newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway March oil output down 5 pct at 3.01 mln bpd.
newsitem.headline: Norway March oil output down 5 pct at 3.01 mln bpd.

text.p: Oil output on the Norwegian continental shelf slipped five percent in March from a month earlier to average 3.01 million barrels per day (bpd), a Reuter survey of operators in Norwegian waters showed.
In February, Norway pumped 3.17 million bpd.
Most of the decline was attributed to sporadic shutdowns at offshore loading fields due to bad weather disrupting tanker loadings causing burgeoning storage.
Throughput was sharply down at the Statfjord field, which added 318,730 bpd to Norwegian output in March compared with 346,922 bpd in February.
Shutdowns at Statfjord also led to decreased output at Snorre and Statfjord East and North satellites.

Gullfaks was less impacted by stormy weather, production slipping nearly three percent to 420,698 bpd versus a month earlier, while production at the Tordis field, which feeds crude to Gullfaks for processing and loading, fell to 66,588 bpd against 75,697 bpd in a month ago.
Shell's Draugen field in the Norwegian Sea also suffered weather-related delays and in addition had a three-day shutdown for a water injection upgrade. Draugen output fell 19 percent to 142,384 bpd.

The new Vigdis development, which came on stream in January, continued to suffer teething problems in March with output averaging 30,437 bpd. Operator Saga Petroleum said the field was now pumping at around plateau of 75,000 bpd.
